title: Pengaruh Kompensasi dan Lingkungan Kerja terhadap Loyalitas Karyawan Swasta di Kabupaten Aceh Barat
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the effect of compensation and work environment on the loyalty of private sector employees in West Aceh Regency. The study employs a quantitative approach using a survey method with 247 respondents. Data were analyzed through validity, reliability, and classical assumption tests, as well as multiple linear regression with robust standard error HC3. The results indicate that compensation has a positive and significant effect on employee loyalty, with a regression coefficient of 0.590 and a significance value of 0.000. The work environment also has a positive and significant effect, with a regression coefficient of 0.340 and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, compensation and work environment significantly influence employee loyalty. The coefficient of determination value of 0.601 indicates that these variables explain 60.1% of employee loyalty, while the remaining 39.9% is explained by other variables outside the research model. These findings confirm that fair compensation and a conducive work environment are important factors in enhancing the loyalty of private sector employees in West Aceh Regency.

title: Cross-Domain Tracing of Rice Stem Stress under Soil Cadmium Pollution
abstractText: Abstract Plants exposed to heavy-metal-contaminated soil are subjected to pollutant pressure, making timely monitoring of plant condition important for assessing their responses to soil pollution. Although spectral sensing is widely used for nondestructive monitoring of plant stress, the cross-domain association between plant optical signals and Cd-induced physiological responses remains unclear. Here, we integrated spectral sensing with deep learning, Monte Carlo simulation, and omics analysis to systematically explore how spectral signals and physiological responses jointly support the monitoring of Cd-induced stress in rice stems. We found that Cd exposure reorganized interface-associated stress, protective chemistry, and redox regulation into coordinated Defense, Repair, and Adjustment signatures. These biological changes were differentially expressed across the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared spectral regions, producing a reweighting of absorption- and scattering-sensitive information. The agreement between spectral variation and biological stress signatures further established a cross-domain link between stress-state formation and optical detection. Benefiting from this mechanism, we achieved high-accuracy nondestructive detection of rice stem Cd content and noninvasive characterization of Cd-induced responses. A portable spectrometer–smartphone implementation further demonstrated field-oriented feasibility. These findings provide a biological and optical basis for tracking stress progression and supporting timely, feedback-guided crop management.

title: Synchronized Twisting, Helical Conformation, and Reduced Symmetry in Alcalde’s Zwitterions: Early Saturation of First Hyperpolarizability before Peierls Distortion
abstractText: Abstract This work reports structure–property correlations for a series of pyridinium imidazolate-based zwitterions. With initial HF/6–31G computations (based on an earlier report: excellent agreement between the experiment and computation), hyperpolarizabilities (β) were found to be abnormally large (β0 ≈ 0.15 million × 10–30 esu and |μβ| ≈ 12 million × 10-48 esu). However, when reinvestigated with the HF, B3LYP, and CAM-B3LYP methodologies (combined with the 6-31G(d,p) basis set), drastic reductions in hyperpolarizabilities were observed. In general, saturations of hyperpolarizabilities were observed with two or three bridging benzene rings (CAM-B3LYP: β0 ≈ 4054.0 × 10–30 esu and |μβ| ≈ 0.2 million × 10–48 esu; although these are among the largest values reported in the literature, they need further experimental verification). Observations of such large hyperpolarizabilities and early saturations were found to occur before the Peierls distortion point. Also, many molecules showed absorptions in near- to far-IR regions, thus capable of providing solutions to the transparency trade-off problem existing in nonlinear optics. Nevertheless, we propose how the gyratory nature of the inter-ring junctions can be synchronized in a helical fashion in a tunable structural topography to control the intramolecular interactions and to induce the optimal hyperpolarizabilities (and saturation limit) and transparency trade-off problem of nonlinear optics.

title: Leading Safety Through Difference: Why Cultural Intelligence Needs a PRISM
abstractText: The health and safety profession has typically focussed on systems, rules, and homogenous approaches to leadership. That thinking has at times been effective, but it has also created pain points for the health and safety professional. Many of the challenges we face today are not because we lack technical knowledge, they show up in our level of understanding of how people work together. Organisational diversity extends beyond the ethnicity of its workers and is seen across culture, experience, and expectations. The pain points experienced by health and safety professionals when faced with this diversity appear in the gaps between how people make decisions, communicate, handle authority, and respond to pressure. We can’t address these challenges by creating more procedures or doing a personality test. This presentation introduces a practical way forward by combining Cultural Intelligence and the emerging PRISM framework. PRISM changes the focus from who people are to how they behave at work. It highlights five observable dimensions: Power, Risk, Identity, Speed, and Messaging. These dimensions shape everyday interactions in ways that either build trust and alignment or create tension and silence. This session demonstrates how misalignment across these dimensions can directly influence safety outcomes, often in ways that go unnoticed. More importantly, it will provide safety professionals with a clear, practical lens to enable them to: Recognise where team dynamics are increasing risk Adapt their leadership approach in real time Apply CQ with greater precision in diverse environments This is not about replacing traditional safety practice but strengthening it. If safety is created through people, then leadership must move beyond the traditional one-size-fits-all approaches. The future of safety depends on our ability to read the room, adjust our approach, and lead effectively across difference.

Prevalence and prognosis of gait dysfunction in patients operated on for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: a Spine CORe™ analysis of QOD data
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Among patients undergoing surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM), the prevalence of gait disturbance and the likelihood of gait improvement remain unclear. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence and prognosis of gait disturbance in CSM and identify factors associated with gait improvement postoperatively. METHODS This was a retrospective analysis of the CSM cohort of the prospectively collected 14-site Spine CORe™ Study Group Quality Outcomes Database (QOD) registry. Outcomes of interest included postoperative ambulatory function at 24 months defined by lower extremity score on the modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scale and predictors of improved ambulation. The p values for descriptive statistics were obtained using paired and unpaired t-tests and chi-square tests as appropriate. For multivariable analysis, a logistic regression model was fit for improvement in gait in the subset of patients with baseline gait impairment. RESULTS Of the 1141 patients meeting prespecified inclusion criteria, 1135 had baseline gait data; of these, 877 (77.3%) had baseline gait dysfunction and 258 (22.7%) did not. At baseline, patients with gait dysfunction were older (61.5 ± 11.6 vs 57.2 ± 11.7 years, p < 0.001), had higher BMI (30.4 ± 6.6 vs 29.3 ± 6.0 kg/m 2 , p = 0.008), were less likely to have private insurance (46.0% vs 67.4%, p < 0.001), and had more comorbidities. Preoperatively, patients with gait dysfunction had worse neck disability (Neck Disability Index [NDI], 41.0 ± 20.8 vs 30.2 ± 18.4, p < 0.001) and quality of life (EQ-VAS, 56.2 ± 21.4 vs 70.0 ± 18.9, p < 0.001; and EQ-5D, 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 0.7 ± 0.2, p < 0.001). Patients with impaired ambulation at baseline were less satisfied with surgery at 24 months (North American Spine Society satisfaction questionnaire [NASS] score 1, 51.4% vs 60.9%, p = 0.004). Among 596 patients with gait dysfunction who received follow-up postoperatively at 24 months, 304 (51.0%) showed improvement and 292 (49.0%) did not. Patients who improved also demonstrated greater improvement in visual analog scale (VAS) neck pain (−3.3 ± 3.2 vs −2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) and arm pain (−3.2 ± 3.9 vs −2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) scores, as well as better NDI (16.5 ± 17.4 vs 26.8 ± 20.9, p < 0.001), EQ-VAS (74.1 ± 20.0 vs 60.2 ± 23.2, p < 0.001), EQ-5D (0.8 ± 0.2 vs 0.6 ± 0.2, p < 0.001), and NASS (score 1, 74.0% vs 53.8%, p < 0.001) scores. Multivariable analyses revealed that lower BMI (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00–1.02, p = 0.01) and lower American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class (for ASA class I or II, OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.04–2.80, p = 0.04) were associated with gait improvement. CONCLUSIONS In this cohort, 77.3% of patients who underwent surgery for CSM demonstrated gait dysfunction preoperatively. Of these patients, 51% had gait improvement after cervical spine surgery. Lower BMI and ASA class were associated with improved gait postoperatively. Patients who improved reported superior quality of life, satisfaction with surgery, and decreased pain and disability.

title: Toward Transferable Descriptors Linking Formation and Environmental Effects of Microplastic-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter
abstractText: Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is increasingly recognized as an active product of plastic weathering; however, its environmental effects remain difficult to compare or predict. A major problem is the absence of variables that can maintain comparable mechanistic meaning across formation and effect studies. To address this gap, we propose a descriptor-based conceptual framework that uses measurable MP-DOM properties as transferable intermediates. Within this framework, using descriptors as a transferable and standardized language, spanning quantity, optical properties, molecular composition, and reactivity, can bridge diverse weathering conditions with downstream environmental effects. Using E2/E3, defined as the absorbance ratio at 250 and 365 nm, as a representative example, we demonstrate how an optical descriptor can connect MP-DOM formation processes with photochemical reactivity and contaminant photodegradation through its relationship with singlet oxygen generation. This framework highlights the need for transferable descriptors as a standardized framework for MP-DOM, providing a foundation for cross-study comparison, mechanistic integration, and predictive assessment of MP-DOM fate and environmental effects.

title: Nomogram for predicting efficacy of repeated intravesical platelet-rich plasma in non-Hunner-type interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome
abstractText: Objectives: To investigate influencing factors and establish a nomogram for predicting the short-term efficacy of repeated intravesical platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections in patients with non-Hunner-type interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 198 patients who completed 4 intravesical PRP injections between February 2023 and June 2025. Treatment efficacy was defined as a Global Response Assessment score ≥2 at 3 months posttreatment. Predictors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and a nomogram was constructed using multivariable logistic regression. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), the Hosmer–Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis, respectively. Bootstrap resampling (B = 1000) was used for internal validation, and a temporal cohort of 52 patients treated between July and December 2025 was used for validation. Results: Of the 198 patients (mean age 56.3 ± 9.5 years; 90.9% female), 127 (64.1%) achieved effective treatment. Longer disease duration (odds ratio [OR], 1.071, p < 0.001), elevated Self-Rating Anxiety Scale score (OR, 1.055, p = 0.001), and concomitant pelvic floor muscle spasm (OR, 7.147, p < 0.001) were risk factors for ineffectiveness; greater maximum bladder capacity (OR = 0.995, p = 0.019) and higher glomerulation grade (OR, 0.421, p = 0.004) were protective factors. The nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.940, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.931 (95% confidence interval, 0.897–0.971) and good calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow χ 2 = 10.23, p = 0.249). Decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.10–0.70. In the temporal validation cohort, the AUC was 0.910 (95% confidence interval, 0.823–0.997). Conclusions: The nomogram demonstrated favorable predictive performance for short-term PRP efficacy in patients with non-Hunner-type interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome and may serve as a decision-support tool for individualized treatment.

title: Extreme heat drives opposing patterns of size-dependent survival across microhabitats
abstractText: Abstract Increasingly frequent and severe heatwaves threaten the persistence of species on Earth. Survival under extreme heat is often attributed to organismal traits, such as body size, yet realized heat exposure also depends on microhabitat. We show that a historical heatwave—which killed over a billion coastal organisms—drove size-dependent survival in an intertidal mussel population, favouring opposite extremes of the size distribution. The direction of size-dependent survival shifted across metre-scale habitat, with small mussels favoured on the high shore but large mussels favoured on the low shore. Dynamic heat flux simulations revealed that body size and microhabitat interact to determine available cooling behaviours, driving the direction of size-dependent survival. On the high shore, greater desiccation risk limited evaporative cooling, advantaging small individuals that cool rapidly via convection (wind-cooling). On the low shore, lower desiccation risk enabled prolonged evaporative cooling, advantaging large-bodied individuals with greater water stores. Climate impact projections focusing primarily on species’ traits may systematically miss predictable, generalizable trait–microhabitat interactions that drive demographic filtering under extreme heat.

title: Revealing Bulk-Phase Reactivity of Fe-Based Catalyst in the Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
abstractText: Abstract Heterogeneous catalysis is conventionally interpreted as a surface-localized process, yet many catalysts undergo extensive reaction-driven restructuring that may fundamentally redistribute reactivity beyond the interface. Here we combine microscopy, isotope-labeling experiments, and large-scale molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP-MD) to investigate reactive carbon–oxygen chemistry in iron catalysts relevant to the reverse water–gas shift reaction. We show that under reaction conditions, the catalyst evolves into a dynamic FeOx/Fe3C mixed phase in which carbon and oxygen continuously redistribute across surface, subsurface and bulk regions. Isotope experiments reveal that bulk carbon is catalytically active, while simulations identify initial C–O association across a broad depth range, including within the catalyst interior, for carbon atoms subsequently removed as CO/CO2. Free-energy calculations characterize representative C–O association pathways at the surface and within the catalyst interior. Together, these results support CO formation beyond conventional surface sites and a surface-to-bulk catalytic picture for dynamically evolving iron catalysts.

دور الإصلاح المؤسسي والحوكمة الرشيدة في دعم الشفافية والمساءلة في الإدارة العامة الليبية "دراسة تحليلية مقارنة في ضوء تجارب دولية مختارة مع تقديم نموذج تطبيقي مقترح"
abstractText: تهدف الدراسة إلى تحليل دور الإصلاح المؤسسي والحوكمة الرشيدة في دعم الشفافية والمساءلة في الإدارة العامة الليبية، واستخلاص الدروس المستفادة من تجارب دولية مختارة، وتكييف الممارسات الملائمة مع خصوصية السياق الليبي، وصولًا إلى تقديم نموذج تطبيقي مقترح لتعزيز الشفافية والمساءلة. اعتمدت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، مدعومًا بالمنهج المقارن، من خلال مراجعة الأدبيات والدراسات السابقة وتحليل الوثائق والتقارير الرقابية المحلية والمؤشرات والتقارير الدولية ذات الصلة، وتشير التقارير الرقابية المحلية والدولية إلى أن الإدارة العامة الليبية تواجه تحديات تتعلق بالتجزؤ المؤسسي، وتداخل الاختصاصات، وفاعلية الرقابة والشفافية، بما يبرز الحاجة إلى إصلاح مؤسسي يعزز التنسيق والمساءلة ويحسن كفاءة الأداء. تشير نتائج التحليل إلى أهمية وضوح المسؤوليات، وتكامل آليات الرقابة الداخلية والخارجية، وتوظيف التحول الرقمي، وتنمية الموارد البشرية، مع التأكيد على أن الاستفادة من التجارب الدولية تتطلب تكييف ممارساتها وفق البيئة التشريعية والمؤسسية الليبية، لا نقلها بصورة حرفية. وبناءً على هذه النتائج، قدمت الدراسة نموذجًا تطبيقيًا مقترحًا لتعزيز الشفافية والمساءلة في الإدارة العامة الليبية، يقوم على تطوير التنسيق المؤسسي، وتوضيح الاختصاصات والمسؤوليات، وتفعيل الرقابة الداخلية، وتحسين الإفصاح وتوثيق الإجراءات الكترونيًا، ومتابعة تنفيذ التوصيات التصحيحية، واعتماد مؤشرات كمية ونوعية لتقييم الأداء، ويُقترح تنفيذ النموذج تدريجيًا عبر مراحل تبدأ بالتشخيص والتهيئة المؤسسية، ثم التطبيق التجريبي والتقييم، وصولًا إلى التوسع في الممارسات الملائمة وفق النتائج والإمكانات المتاحة. توصي الدراسة بتطوير الأطر التشريعية والتنظيمية، وتعزيز استقلالية الوظائف الرقابية، وتفعيل آليات الشكاوى والتظلمات، وتأهيل القيادات والموظفين، وإجراء تقييمات دورية لقياس التقدم في تطبيق الحوكمة والإصلاح المؤسسي. تتمثل القيمة المضافة للدراسة في الربط بين التحليل النظري والمقارنة الدولية والتصميم التطبيقي المقترح، مع مراعاة خصوصية الإدارة العامة الليبية، على أن فاعلية النموذج المقترح وقابليته للتنفيذ والاستدامة تظل بحاجة إلى اختبار ميداني وتقييم عملي.

title: Stemness-associated transcriptional profiles reveal prognostic and microenvironmental heterogeneity in osteosarcoma
abstractText: Background Osteosarcoma (OS) is an aggressive primary bone malignancy with poor outcomes in patients with recurrent or metastatic disease. Although molecular profiling has revealed substantial heterogeneity in OS, the relationships between stemness-associated gene expression, patient prognosis, and the tumor immune microenvironment remain incompletely understood. Methods In this study, non-negative matrix factorization of stemness-associated gene expression was used to identify molecular subtypes in TARGET-OS. Functional enrichment, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, somatic mutation profiling, and drug response prediction characterized subtype differences. After joint batch correction of TARGET-OS and GSE21257, an overall survival model based on stemness-associated gene expression was developed using LASSO and Cox regression in TARGET-OS and evaluated in GSE21257. Immune infiltration and single-cell transcriptomic analyses characterized the associated immune features, cellular distribution of the signature, and potential cell–cell interactions. Results Our analysis identified two exploratory stemness-associated OS subtypes with distinct prognoses in the TARGET-OS cohort. C1 showed poorer survival and enrichment of metabolic and DNA repair programs, whereas C2 was enriched for extracellular matrix and immune-related processes. Drug response predictions indicated greater sensitivity to fixed-ratio combinations containing selumetinib in C1 and to cabozantinib in C2. We developed a nine-gene signature that stratified overall survival in both cohorts, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs of 0.653, 0.751, and 0.711, respectively, in GSE21257. High-risk tumors exhibited lower immune scores and reduced estimated infiltration of CD8 + T Cells and B Cells. Single-cell analysis revealed relatively high signature scores in OS cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts. The high-scoring OS1 subpopulation was enriched for ossification and extracellular matrix-related processes. Communication analysis further predicted COL1A1–CD44 interactions from OS cells and fibroblasts to monocytes. Conclusion Our study characterizes stemness-associated transcriptional heterogeneity in OS and identifies a nine-gene prognostic signature. These findings associate survival differences with metabolic and immune programs and reveal the cellular expression patterns of the signature in tumor and stromal cells.

Condiciones laborales y salud mental del personal de Enfermería en México durante la pandemia Covid-19
abstractText: Nursing staff faced working conditions that impacted their mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic. Objective: To analyze the relationship between working conditions and mental health—burnout, anxiety, and depression—among nursing staff in Mexico during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methodology: A descriptive cross-sectional study using online surveys to assess working conditions and mental health. Results: 81.1% reported an emotional disturbance. Anxiety was the most common (60%), followed by burnout (40%) and depression (30%). 8.8% reported all three conditions simultaneously, and 94.8% reported job satisfaction. The models (logistic regression and Random Forest) highlighted that exposure to environmental risks, physical exertion, and a lack of material resources exacerbated symptoms. Conclusion: The evidence points to the need for structural interventions; institutional policies are required to improve working conditions and implement psychosocial support, especially for young staff and those in critical areas.

Mức độ phơi nhiễm chì mạn tính và mối liên quan với việc sử dụng phương tiện bảo vệ cá nhân tại làng nghề đúc đồng Lộng Thượng, Hưng Yên năm 2025
abstractText: Tại các làng nghề đúc đồng, quá trình sản xuất thủ công phát sinh lượng lớn hơi chì, trong khi việc sử dụng phương tiện bảo vệ cá nhân (PPE) kém hiệu quả có thể gia tăng rủi ro phơi nhiễm qua “nghịch lý bảo hộ”. Nghiên cứu này nhằm đánh giá mức độ phơi nhiễm chì mạn tính và phân tích mối liên quan với việc sử dụng PPE để làm rõ hiện tượng trên tại làng nghề Lộng Thượng, Hưng Yên năm 2025. Thông qua thiết kế mô tả cắt ngang, nghiên cứu tiến hành chọn mẫu toàn bộ 89 người lao động trực tiếp và thu thập 20 mẫu không khí. Dữ liệu phỏng vấn, quan trắc môi trường và định lượng chì máu được phân tích thống kê bằng kiểm định Mann-Whitney U và hồi quy tuyến tính logarithm. Kết quả chỉ ra nồng độ hơi chì tại khu vực gia công có 4/10 mẫu vượt quy chuẩn, cực đại đạt 1,35 mg/m³. Nồng độ chì máu trung vị của quần thể là 11,78 µg/dL, với 64,0% đối tượng vượt ngưỡng cho phép. Phân tích làm sáng tỏ hiện tượng nghịch lý bảo hộ khi nhóm sử dụng khẩu trang vải và găng tay sợi có nồng độ chì máu cao hơn có ý nghĩa thống kê so với nhóm không sử dụng (khẩu trang: 12,1 so với 8,3 µg/dL, p=0,034; găng tay: 12,3 so với 10,3 µg/dL, p=0,032). Tóm lại, sản xuất đúc đồng thủ công tiềm ẩn rủi ro phơi nhiễm chì rất cao, việc tái sử dụng PPE không đạt chuẩn cùng thực hành vệ sinh kém đã biến các phương tiện này thành nguồn lây nhiễm độc chất thứ cấp. Cần khẩn trương áp dụng các biện pháp kiểm soát kỹ thuật và tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt chuẩn mực an toàn vệ sinh lao động.

Liver Disease in Older Adults: Diagnosis, Management, and Transplantations
abstractText: Abstract Purpose of Review To summarize age-specific considerations in the diagnosis and management of liver disease in adults aged 65 years and older, with emphasis on cirrhosis, liver transplantation, frailty, and cognitive impairment. Recent Findings Age alters the performance and tolerability of commonly used diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Age-adjusted interpretation of serum fibrosis tests, sequential use of elastography, careful titration of cirrhosis therapies, and routine frailty assessment can reduce avoidable harm. Transplant outcomes in carefully selected older recipients remain acceptable, and chronological age alone should not determine candidacy. Summary The care of the older adults with liver disease should integrate disease severity with physiologic reserve, comorbidity, function, medication safety, and cognition. A structured evaluation is particularly important when hepatic encephalopathy overlaps with delirium or dementia.

Desarrollo y validación de una herramienta independiente de cálculo redundante para la dosimetría en braquiterapia de alta tasa de dosis
abstractText: Se ha desarrollado un programa de cálculo redundante de dosis (PCRD) para la verificación dosimétrica en braquiterapia de alta tasa de dosis (HDR), en el marco del Real Decreto 391/2025. El software implementa el formalismo TG-43 y utiliza como datos de entrada la información contenida en los ficheros DICOM exportados desde el sistema de planificación, lo que permite una verificación automatizada y transparente. Su validación mostró discrepancias inferiores al ±2% respecto a tablas de consenso y al sistema de planificación (TPS) comercial Oncentra Brachy. En 433 tratamientos clínicos reales se obtuvo una concordancia casi perfecta (CCC > 0.99), y discrepancias dentro de los límites de tolerancia establecidos. Además, el programa permite cuantificar el impacto de desplazamientos sistemáticos y aleatorios de los catéteres sobre el cálculo dosimétrico. El PCRD constituye una herramienta precisa y clínicamente aplicable para reforzar la seguridad y calidad de los tratamientos de braquiterapia HDR.

title: Assessing quality of life during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injuries
abstractText: OBJECTIVE The objective of this study was to assess quality of life (QOL) outcomes during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injury (BPBI) and to identify factors linked to poorer outcomes. Additionally, the authors aimed to determine the construct validity of the Impact of a Brachial Plexus Injury Questionnaire (Mancuso scale) for use in the birth injury population. METHODS This study utilized a cross-sectional, within-subject comparative survey design to assess the QOL outcomes of adolescents and adults with BPBI. Participants older than 13 years of age and with a history of BPBI were identified using the United Brachial Plexus Network Facebook group. QOL was assessed using the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale–Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) in adults, Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) in adolescents, and a brachial plexus injury–specific tool (Mancuso scale). To determine construct validity, scores from each Mancuso subscale were compared to the participants’ overall WHOQOL-BREF scores. RESULTS Adults (n = 59) who completed the WHOQOL-BREF had a mean overall score of 63.1 ± 22.2 (0- to 100-point scale). The scores of the Mancuso scale with regard to the symptoms, limitations, and emotion subscales were 45.8 ± 29.5, 35.2 ± 17.3, and 43.6 ± 25.3, respectively. These findings contrasted with the published values from subjects who had sustained a traumatic brachial plexus injury whose scores were 66 ± 18.7, 48.2 ± 22.3, and 39.5 ± 21.2, respectively. For adolescents (n = 4), the overall score on PedsQL was 63.7 ± 21.3. Adolescent scores on the Mancuso scale were 31.7 ± 26.9, 29.8 ± 20.7, and 39.7 ± 18.8, respectively. In adults, severe functional limitation and limited access to care were associated with poorer QOL (p < 0.05), whereas surgical history and occupational therapy attendance did not. Higher scores on the Mancuso subscales correlated with lower quality of life scores on the WHOQOL-BREF. Adolescent data analysis revealed similar, nonsignificant results. CONCLUSIONS BPBI plays a role in long-term QOL, notably by the severity of functional limitation and access to care. The Mancuso scale shows promising construct validity in the adult BPBI population, but a larger sample of adolescents is needed.

Why dreamcore appeals to nostalgic individuals: the role of authenticity-related self-experience
abstractText: Abstract Background Dreamcore is an emerging visual aesthetic that circulates across social media platforms and combines nostalgic familiarity with dreamlike, displaced, and sometimes unsettling imagery. Dreamcore has gained increasing attention in online visual culture; however, it remains poorly understood why some people find this familiar yet unfamiliar imagery appealing. The present study examined whether Dreamcore liking is linked to trait nostalgia through authenticity-related self-experience. Methods Chinese participants aged 18–40 years ( N = 449) completed measures of trait nostalgia, three facets of authenticity, and Dreamcore image liking. Dreamcore liking was modeled as two latent dimensions: Warm Dreamcore liking and Eerie Dreamcore liking. A latent structural equation model was used to examine indirect associations between trait nostalgia, authenticity facets, and Dreamcore liking. Results Trait nostalgia was positively associated with all three authenticity facets. Authentic Living was positively associated with both Warm and Eerie Dreamcore liking and showed significant indirect associations linking trait nostalgia to both liking dimensions. Self-Alienation was associated with Eerie Dreamcore liking, whereas its association with Warm Dreamcore liking was not statistically supported; however, the contrast analysis did not support that its link to Eerie Dreamcore liking was stronger than its link to Warm Dreamcore liking. Accepting External Influence was not uniquely associated with either outcome. Conclusions Associations between trait nostalgia and Dreamcore image liking were partly reflected in indirect links through authenticity-related self-experience, particularly Authentic Living, suggesting that the appeal of such imagery may depend not only on its nostalgia-related affective qualities, but also on self-congruent experience. More broadly, self-related individual differences may be relevant to responses to Dreamcore and related emerging online-popular digital aesthetics, with implications for further research on self-relevance, aesthetic experience, and contemporary digital culture.

title: UNITY THROUGH SERIAL DESIGN: ROW STRUCTURE, B-A-C-H MOTIVIC PROCESSES, AND TONAL REFERENCES IN SIMBOLO FROM LUIGI DALLAPICCOLA'S QUADERNO MUSICALE DI ANNALIBERA
abstractText: Background and Objectives: This research article presents an in-depth theoretical and structural analysis of Simbolo, the first movement of Luigi Dallapiccola's 1952 solo piano collection, Quaderno Musicale di Annalibera. Composed for the Pittsburgh International Contemporary Music Festival and dedicated to the composer's daughter, the collection consists of eleven short pieces unified entirely by a single twelve-tone row. Notably, the collection is intended to be performed in its entirety rather than existing solely for pedagogical purposes, and Dallapiccola later repurposed this exact twelve-tone series in major works like Canti di Liberazione and Quaderno: Variazioni per orchestra. The primary objective of this study is to examine the specific serial techniques Dallapiccola employs within Simbolo, with a specialized focus on row organization, motivic permutations, the prominent role of the B-A-C-H motive, and the seamless integration of tonal references within a strict dodecaphonic framework. Methods: The study systematically breaks down the twelve-tone foundation of the work by mapping the complete twelve-tone matrix and detailing the specific sequence of row forms that structure the piece, starting with the basic tone row (P0: Bb-B-Eb-Gb-Ab-D-Db-F-G-C-A-E). Furthermore, the analysis explores the formal structure of Simbolo by examining distinct shifts in articulation, tempo alterations, textural variations, and fluid time signature changes. The structural and thematic role of the four-note B-A-C-H motive (B-flat, A, C, and B-natural) is traced through its exact original statements, retrogrades, inversions, and retrograde-inversions across the composition. Additional methods include analyzing harmonic sonorities to identify triadic relationships and evaluating dynamic markings in relation to row deployments. Results: The analysis reveals that the basic tone row (P0) serves as a definitive framing device, utilized at both the opening and the conclusion of the piece. The B-A-C-H motive is inherently embedded within this primary row—for example, the P form presents it transposed to Eb-D-F-E—and acts as a paramount unifying element. The B-A-C-H motive recurs throughout the movement in its original, retrograde, inversion, and retrograde-inversion forms, together with additional permutations and reorderings of its pitch-class collection, including circular permutation. Formally, the piece follows a clear A-B-A' ternary structure (A: mm. 1-16, B: mm. 17-36, A': mm. 37-46), delineated by contrasting phrasing, dynamics, and alternating accompaniment patterns. The climax occurs between measures 25 and 29, reaching the highest pitch (Bb) and loudest dynamic (mf). The study highlights that frequent time signature changes (e.g., 3/4, 7/8, 6/8, 5/8) and specific dynamic shifts directly correspond with and signal the arrival of new row forms. Most significantly, pronounced tonal references coexist alongside these rigorous serial procedures. Tonal implications are projected through pedal points, triad-implying hexachords (such as B-major and A-minor-seventh chords), and local tonic-dominant allusions, evidenced by an Eb minor triad moving to a dominant-functioning Bb seventh chord, and by a cadence-like gesture in which a G half-diminished seventh resolves by stepwise voice leading into the closing A minor triad. Conclusions: Ultimately, these findings thoroughly illustrate Dallapiccola's highly distinctive and expressive approach to twelve-tone composition. A profound sense of unity is achieved through the symmetrical framing of the P0 row, the identical five-measure counts in the opening and closing statements, and the pervasive development of the historical B-A-C-H motive. By brilliantly synthesizing strict serial techniques with traditional tonal implications, Dallapiccola successfully creates an organically cohesive and unified musical structure.

title: A Sociolegal Study of Marriage Registrars’ Implementation of The Circular on Remarriage During a Former Wife’s Iddah
abstractText: Background/Introduction: Administrative guidance on remarriage during a former wife’s iddah raises questions about legal interpretation and consistency in marriage registration. Research Objectives: This study examines registrars’ interpretations of the circular’s binding force, their reported handling considerations, and differences in application outcomes in Magetan Regency. Methodology: An exploratory qualitative study employed an empirical legal approach and a sociology-of-law perspective. Data comprised preliminary Google Forms responses from 18 registrars, supported by legal materials and scholarly literature. Analysis drew on Friedman’s legal system framework and Lipsky’s street-level bureaucracy perspective. Results: Eight KUA offices reported ten relevant applications during 2024–October 2026. Five reportedly resulted in postponement until iddah ended, while five proceeded before its reported completion. Registrars reported knowing the guidance and requesting postponement but expressed different interpretations of administrative authority and family circumstances. Case documents remain independently unverified, and attribution and chronological discrepancies limit interpretation. Unique Contribution: The study distinguishes reported policy knowledge, interpretive orientations, and application outcomes without assuming a direct causal relationship. Conclusion: Reported awareness of the circular did not always lead to postponement. However, the evidence does not establish the effectiveness of implementation or the legal validity of individual decisions. Recommendations: Authorities should clarify consultation procedures and strengthen decision documentation. Further research should verify case records and incorporate applicants’ and former spouses’ perspectives.

Dynamic Behavior of Single-Atom Palladium-Ceria Nanoparticles on γ-Al2O3
abstractText: Abstract Herein, Pd single-atom catalysts are embedded within nanoscale CeO2 nanoparticles, which are further stabilized on a secondary γ-Al2O3 support. High-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and pair distribution function analyses reveal that Pd(II) atoms occupy square-planar sites within the fluorite lattice of the CeO2, forming Ce1–xPdxO2−δ solid-state solutions. Electron microscopy showed that these nanoscale Ce1–xPdxO2−δ domains are uniformly dispersed across the γ-Al2O3 support, while solid-state NMR confirms their anchoring through under-coordinated Al-sites. Under alternating oxidizing and reducing environments, the catalyst undergoes a reversible structural evolution of Pd speciation and coordination environment. These findings reveal a dynamic solid-state structural evolution of the Ce1–xPdxO2−δ phase on the surface of γ-Al2O3 supports. Notably, Pd nanoclusters generated by CO treatment of the Ce1–xPdxO2−δ solid-state solutions exhibited the earliest onset of CO oxidation activity, highlighting the catalytic significance of this structural evolution.

title: Green Tea Catechins in Cancer Prevention and Therapy: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, Safety, and Future Perspectives
abstractText: Green tea, derived from Camellia sinensis, is a widely consumed dietary source of bioactive polyphenols. Among its major catechins, epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) has been studied most extensively in cancer research. This review critically synthesizes phytochemical, molecular, preclinical, epidemiological, clinical, pharmacokinetic, and safety evidence to assess the potential role of green tea catechins in cancer prevention and treatment. Preclinical studies of breast, prostate, colorectal, lung, liver, oral, and hematological cancers indicate that EGCG modulates oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, proliferation, apoptosis, cell-cycle progression, angiogenesis, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, invasion, metastasis, and epigenetic regulation. Reported molecular targets include the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, MAPK, JAK–STAT, and NF-κB signaling pathways, as well as EGFR and VEGF signaling, BCL-2 family proteins, caspases, matrix metalloproteinases, and enzymes involved in DNA methylation. A systematic review and meta-analysis reported an association between green tea or EGCG exposure and lower overall cancer risk, with variation by cancer type and study design. Clinical evidence for efficacy in established malignancies remains limited, and conventional oncological treatment remains the standard of care. By integrating mechanistic findings with human data, this review identifies gaps in clinical efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and safety that must be addressed before green tea catechins can be incorporated into evidence-based oncology.

title: A bio-digital circular framework for sustainable duck feed production using agro-industrial side-streams and aquatic biomass
abstractText: Abstract The poultry sector faces increasing environmental and economic pressures associated with agro-industrial by-product accumulation, dependence on conventional feed ingredients, and feed-supply logistics. This study developed the SHIREEM framework, a bio-digital circular approach for the valorization of Snack Food Industry By-products (SFIB) and aquatic biomass ( Azolla pinnata and Spirulina platensis ) in poultry feed production. The framework integrates IoT-assisted process monitoring, computational feed optimization, machine-learning prediction, and circular resource-utilization principles. An IoT-assisted pelleting system incorporating a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and real-time sensors was used to monitor and control processing conditions, while a Python-based Least-Cost Ration (LCR) model optimized feed formulations under predefined nutritional and economic constraints. Under the simulated conditions, the optimized formulation reduced the estimated feed production cost from approximately 22,000 to 12,450 EGP ton⁻¹ (43.4%) and reduced logistics-related CO₂ emissions by 93.8% within the defined assessment boundary. Machine-learning models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with Gradient Boosting providing the best prediction of body weight and Extra-Trees providing the best prediction of feed conversion ratio among the evaluated models. Feature-importance analysis indicated that age and metabolizable energy were major predictors of growth-related performance, whereas Azolla inclusion showed a greater contribution to feed conversion ratio than to body weight prediction. In addition, 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation indicated that the economic performance of the optimized system remained feasible across the majority of the simulated uncertainty scenarios, with SFIB cost and transportation expenditure identified as important cost drivers. Overall, the results support the potential of SHIREEM as an integrated computational framework for circular feed-resource utilization and localized production. However, the findings represent a computational proof-of-concept and require experimental and commercial-scale validation before biological, environmental, and economic performance can be generalized to practical poultry production systems. To support regional adoption, agricultural policymakers could consider developing appropriate quality-certification frameworks for bio-based feed resources and supportive policy mechanisms that facilitate the responsible upcycling of locally available agro-industrial residues into animal feed.

abstractText: Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu là mô tả thực trạng tiêu thụ ực phẩm và khẩu phần ăn ở trẻ 6-23 tháng tuổi tại xã Xuân Thới Thượng (nay thuộc xã Bà Điểm), thành phố Hồ Chí Minh năm 2025. Trong khi các nguồn đạm thực vật và trứng ít được sử dụng (tỷ lệ tương ứng 6,0% và 14,0%), tỷ lệ tiêu thụ đồ uống có đường (42,0%) và thực phẩm không lành mạnh (24,0%) lại ở mức cao. abstractText: Education should not only focus on knowledge acquisition but also support the integrated development of intellectual intelligence (IQ), emotional intelligence (EQ), and spiritual intelligence (SQ). This study aims to analyze the role of teachers in supporting the development of these three dimensions of intelligence through the local wisdom concept of Tri Hita Karana in Hindu Religious Education and Character Education at SMK Negeri 2 Kuta Selatan. This study employed a qualitative descriptive approach. Informants were selected using purposive sampling, consisting of eight participants: one Hindu Religious Education and Character Education teacher and seven twelfth-grade students from the Culinary Skills Concentration. Data were collected through participatory observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews, documentation, and literature review. Data analysis involved data collection, data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that the teacher integrates the values of Tri Hita Karana through lesson planning, material explanation, question-and-answer sessions, discussions, and connections between learning materials, daily life, and religious activities. However, its implementation faces several challenges, including theoretical learning materials, limited learning resources and media, time constraints, and uneven student participation. The implications of learning indicate potential development in the intellectual dimension through contextual understanding, the emotional dimension through cooperation and social awareness, and the spiritual dimension through religious awareness and participation in religious activities. Nevertheless, these developments have not yet been optimal or consistent. Therefore, learning needs to be supported by more interactive teaching methods, direct experiences, reflection, and the continuous habituation of local wisdom values.

Primary spinal bone tumors presenting as foraminal nerve sheath lesions: illustrative cases
abstractText: BACKGROUND Dumbbell-shaped foraminal lesions are usually benign nerve sheath tumors, but primary bone tumors can adopt the same silhouette. When they do, preoperative imaging is often misread as a schwannoma and oncological therapy is delayed. OBSERVATIONS Five patients (2 women, ages 25–66 years) had cervical (n = 2), thoracic (n = 2), or lumbosacral (n = 1) lesions interpreted as benign nerve sheath tumors on MRI. On CT, available in 4 cases, each lesion showed cortical breach or expansile lysis that had not altered the initial diagnosis. Final pathological analysis revealed vertebral hemangioma (n = 2), giant cell tumor of bone (n = 1), synovial sarcoma (n = 1), and undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (n = 1). Gross-total resection was achieved in 4 patients. At a median 7-month follow-up, 4 patients improved neurologically and 1 remained stable; the synovial sarcoma recurred locally and was salvaged with revision surgery and chemoradiation therapy. LESSONS Cortical discontinuity, matrix mineralization, or a disproportionately large extraspinal soft tissue component on imaging of a foraminal dumbbell lesion warrants dedicated CT and multidisciplinary review before resection to preserve oncological margins and neurological function. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26428

title: Advances in green and low-energy carbon capture key technologies toward engineering applications
abstractText: Within the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework, green and low-energy CO2 capture technologies are essential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and achieve carbon neutrality. As global carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) demonstration scales continue to expand, chemical absorption using amine solvents has emerged as the industrial benchmark. However, high energy consumption and poor solvent stability hinder large-scale deployment, while secondary pollution from solvent degradation and amine emissions poses a critical barrier to the green and sustainable development of this technology. To overcome these limitations, research efforts in the CO2 capture field have increasingly focused on the synergistic integration of process intensification and materials innovation. This review summarizes recent advances in green and low-energy CO2 capture technologies for engineering applications. The review first presents mainstream process optimization strategies currently adopted in the CO2 capture industry. Building on this, the development and application of novel green and low-energy CO2 capture systems are discussed in detail, encompassing enzymatic absorption and phase-change absorption systems. Furthermore, catalytic desorption technology is identified as a critical enabler for driving the green transformation of conventional amine-based CO2 capture processes. By analyzing the underlying mechanisms, material selection, and process compatibility, future research directions are briefly discussed. This review aims to guide research, development, and engineering deployment of green, low-energy CO2 capture technologies.

title: “Enhancing Kedah–Perlis Border Security: An Intrusion Model with the General Operations Force”
abstractText: Despite continuous efforts by the General Operations Force (GOF) to secure the Kedah–Perlis borders—through measures such as border patrols, advanced surveillance, and joint operations with other enforcement agencies—significant challenges remain in regulating entries into Malaysia. These challenges are particularly evident in both lawful and unlawful crossings, as well as in combating smuggling and human trafficking. The situation is further exacerbated by porous borders and transnational crimes, often orchestrated by criminal syndicates and individuals. While existing research has explored various aspects of border security, there remains a notable gap in developing a comprehensive model that captures the broader scope of these issues and the specific management techniques employed by GOF at the Kedah-Perlis border. This study addresses the existing gap by developing and proposing a holistic conceptual framework known as the Border Security Intrusion Model. Derived from the analysis of empirical data, the model encompasses five stages: (a) intrusion, (b) mechanisms of intrusion, (c) locations of intrusion, (d) purposes of intrusion, and (e) countermeasures against intrusion. The study examines the primary motivations behind intrusions into the land borders of Kedah and Perlis, the methods by which these intrusions are carried out, their most frequent locations, the purposes they serve, and the countermeasures implemented by GOF to address them. This study employs a case study approach by reviewing the perspectives of GOF officials as primary sources, highlighting field best practices and potential enhancements to border enforcement strategies at the Kedah-Perlis border. The analysis demonstrates that the Border Security Intrusion Model offers a broader provides a bigger picture of understanding of border security issues in the region, identifying the root causes of these problems and the countermeasures applied to address such threats. Furthermore, the study outlines the operational mechanisms engaged by GOF in safeguarding the Kedah–Perlis borders against emerging threats.

title: Humidity-Regulated MOF-Kirigami Passive Flyer
abstractText: Abstract While passive flyers have gained increasing attention as an energy-efficient alternative to active unmanned aerial vehicles, they are challenged by limited flight time, high energy consumption, and large-scale deployment issues caused by heavy batteries and complex electronics. The dandelion seed, a natural passive flyer for wind-borne dispersal, has inspired the design of synthetic biomimetic counterparts that similarly leverage airflow for sustained locomotion. However, existing designs lack adaptive mechanisms to respond to diverse environmental conditions such as humidity variation, limiting their functionality in real-world atmospheres. Thus, a humidity-regulated passive flyer was presented here which integrates a ZPF-2-Co metal-organic framework (MOF)-polymer composite humidity actuator into a dandelion-seed-inspired kirigami structure. This flyer is capable of altering its flight position based on ambient humidity, enabling adaptive dispersal. A theoretical model about descent of a dandelion seed was established, using fluid dynamics simulations to analyze the flow field and pressure distribution. It is revealed that a vortex ring formed above the pappus increases drag and slows descent, while a restoring torque stabilizes the attitude and enables gliding upon tilt. Flight tests under seven humidity conditions reveal that the flyer descends vertically below 70% RH, transitions into stable gliding between 70% and 80% RH for controlled long-distance dispersal, and loses gliding stability due to flipping when RH exceeds 84.6%. The passive flyers developed in this work validate the humidity-regulating functionality of MOFs and their potential implementation in flexible devices, providing a foundation for future applications such as smart agriculture, distributed environmental sensing, and pollution tracking.

Provider and Administrator Perspectives on Barriers, Facilitators and Frontline Adaptations in Antenatal Care Delivery in Rural Primary Health Centres in Gujarat, India: A Qualitative Descriptive Study
abstractText: Introduction: Higher antenatal care (ANC) coverage does not guarantee timely, complete and continuous care. We explored how frontline providers and district administrators perceive and manage health-system constraints on ANC delivery in lower-performing rural Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in Gujarat, India. Methods: We conducted a qualitative descriptive study in Bhavnagar district from January 2021 to February 2023. PHCs were purposively selected, prioritising lower-performing facilities. We conducted 34 interviews in total, comprising 32 in-depth interviews with 10 medical officers, 12 female health workers, and 10 accredited social health activists, along with two key-informant interviews with district officials. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed and translated. Two investigators independently coded transcripts and developed themes inductively; themes were then mapped to Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) domains and WHO health-system building blocks. Results: Six themes emerged: service readiness; workforce capacity; information and diagnostics; community engagement; governance and supervision; and frontline adaptability. Participants described a recurring sequence in which structural constraints produced operational consequences (repeated visits, delayed decisions, congestion, referral difficulty); frontline workers responded through ASHA follow-up, due lists, flexible scheduling, outreach and local problem-solving; and these responses reduced but did not close the underlying gaps. Conclusion: Constraints were experienced as interacting rather than isolated problems. Frontline adaptive practices buffered some operational effects but could not substitute for structural capacity. Findings are context-specific, rest on provider and administrator perspectives, and are hypothesis-generating.

Photobiomodulation (low-level laser therapy) for temporomandibular disorders: clinical efficacy, methodological quality, and dosimetric reporting — an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
abstractText: Abstract Background To synthesise, at the level of systematic reviews (SRs) and meta-analyses (MAs), the efficacy of photobiomodulation (PBM)/low-level laser therapy (LLLT) for temporomandibular disorders (TMD), and to appraise the corpus’s methodological quality (AMSTAR-2), primary-study overlap, and dosimetry reporting. Methods Umbrella review of SRs/MAs of PBM/LLLT for TMD (PROSPERO: CRD420261458816). Five databases (Epistemonikos, PubMed/MEDLINE, Lens.org, LILACS, SciELO) were searched from inception to 25 July 2026 without language restriction. Quality was appraised with AMSTAR-2, overlap via corrected covered area (CCA), and dosimetry against a checklist; synthesis was narrative, and certainty was rated with GRADE using the estimates reported by the source meta-analyses. Results Of 231 records, 136 were unique and 32 SRs/MAs met inclusion. Most pooled estimates favoured PBM for short-term pain and maximum mouth opening (MMO; e.g., pain SMD − 0.55, 95% CI − 0.82 to − 0.27, Hanna 2021; MMO MD + 2.78 mm, 1.12 to 4.44, Máximo 2022), but magnitude was highly heterogeneous (I² up to 99%) and metrics non-comparable. Of 30 appraisable, 21 were AMSTAR-2 “Critically Low”, 1 “High”; just 11/32 reported a registered protocol. Across 30 reviews with retrievable study lists, 180 primary trials underpinned the corpus (45% included in ≥ 2 reviews); overall overlap was slight (CCA 5.48%). Wavelength and schedule were reported by 94%, but power density/irradiance (41%) and energy/dose (44%) in fewer than half. Conclusions PBM/LLLT may reduce temporomandibular pain (low certainty, GRADE), but the evidence is very uncertain about the effect on short-term mouth opening (very low certainty), and harms were not assessed. The review-level evidence is numerous but shows only slight primary-study overlap, is mostly of critically low methodological quality, and is inconsistent in reporting delivered-dose parameters. Pre-registered trials that report complete dosimetry would allow future syntheses to estimate the effect and its dose dependence more reliably. Registration PROSPERO CRD420261458816.

Alnustone promotes hepatic stellate cell ferroptosis via the DNMT3A/GLS2/SLC7A11 axis
abstractText: Abstract Liver fibrosis is a progressive pathological process driven by chronic liver injury, with hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation as its core driver. Ferroptosis has been demonstrated to mediate HSC activation, and accumulating evidence indicates that GLS2 and DNMT3A play key regulatory roles in ferroptosis. Consequently, targeting ferroptosis has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy. Alnustone, a natural diarylheptanoid, exhibits anti-fibrotic potential and hepatoprotective properties. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the anti-fibrotic effects of alnustone and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. The results revealed that alnustone significantly attenuated CCl 4 -induced liver fibrosis in mice, as evidenced by reduced serum liver injury markers, collagen deposition, and downregulated HSC activation markers (α-SMA, Col1A1). RNA-sequencing and functional experiments confirmed that alnustone induced HSC ferroptosis in vivo and in vitro, characterized by mitochondrial cristae loss and elevated ferroptosis hallmarks. The ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 abrogated alnustone’s HSC-inactivating effects in vitro. Mechanistically, alnustone targeted and suppressed DNMT3A expression, promoting GLS2 demethylation and upregulation. Co-IP and molecular docking confirmed that GLS2 interacted with SLC7A11 to negatively regulate its expression, thereby facilitating HSC ferroptosis. In addition, DNMT3A overexpression reversed alnustone-induced GLS2 upregulation and ferroptosis. Silencing GLS2 suppressed alnustone-induced HSC ferroptosis and inactivation, whereas GLS2 overexpression alleviated liver fibrosis in HSC-specific GLS2-overexpression (GLS2 cKI ) mice after CCl 4 treatment. Collectively, alnustone alleviates liver fibrosis by inducing HSC ferroptosis through the DNMT3A/GLS2/SLC7A11 axis.

title: Exploring Autonomous Learning in High-Achieving EFL Students: Cases of Success
abstractText: This multiple-case study explored how high-achieving English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students develop and implement autonomous learning practices and how they perceive the contribution of these practices to their academic and competitive achievement. Four students of SMA Negeri 1 Dampit, who were in grades X and XI in the 2025/2026 academic year, were purposively selected: each had an English report-card score of at least 85 in the even semester and a top-three placement or special award in an English competition at university level or at least regency level. Each student was treated as one case. Data came from asynchronous WhatsApp interviews (written messages and voice notes) and document analysis of report cards and certificates, and were analyzed through six-phase thematic analysis with within-case and cross-case comparison. Five themes emerged: developing autonomous learning habits; self-regulated learning strategies; technology-supported autonomous learning; competition-oriented learning practices; and perceived contribution of autonomy. The participants perceived autonomous learning as an important contributor to their success in English competitions and their school performance. However, their learning practices also involved support from family members, teachers, mentors, and school clubs. These findings suggest that autonomous learning among high-achieving students can take different forms and develop alongside support from others.

title: Energy–Dose Optimization and Substrate Effects in Ion-Induced Graphene Nanopore Creation
abstractText: Abstract Ion irradiation of graphene involves a trade-off among controlled nanopore formation, collateral defect generation, and retained mechanical integrity. Here, molecular dynamics simulations are used to establish a first-order quantitative guideline linking ion energy, ion dose, and target pore geometry for argon-ion-induced nanopore formation in free-standing graphene. By mapping this coupled dependence, we identify the threshold conditions for complete pore opening and the energetically favorable pathways toward prescribed pore sizes. Substrate thickness and substrate type are found to alter sputtering through two competing mechanisms: at low and intermediate energies, the substrate suppresses net damage by limiting atom escape and promoting rapid recombination, whereas at higher energies, recoil and backscattering enhance carbon displacement. We further show that the mechanical strength of nanoporous graphene is strongly reduced when irradiation-induced defects form near the pore edge, because of amplified local stress concentration and earlier crack initiation. These results provide a unified description of pore opening thresholds, energy optimization, substrate-mediated damage evolution, and defect-controlled mechanical weakening in ion-irradiated graphene.

title: A new species of Delia Robineau-Desvoidy (Diptera: Anthomyiidae) from Colombia, with a key to Neotropical species
abstractText: Root maggot flies (Delia Robineau-Desvoidy) are polyphagous, and some species are important agricultural pests of commercially relevant crops. The taxonomy of the genus is challenging due to morphological similarity among species, often requiring examination of male terminalia for reliable identification. In South America, the biodiversity of Delia species remains insufficiently understood. A new species of the genus originating from the Páramo and Andean Forest ecosystems of the Eastern Andes mountain range in Colombia is described. Namely, Delia sibatensis sp. nov. (type locality: Sibaté, Vereda Romeral). Since the new species was frequently observed coming into contact with anthers and/or stigmas of strawberry flowers during their receptive period, and as it was found to carry strawberry pollen on its body during observation, it could be a potential pollinator of these crops. Taxonomic, morphological, molecular, and geographic distribution aspects of D. sibatensis sp. nov. are provided. In addition, an identification key to Neotropical species is provided.

Beyond the tool: what a course-aligned AI assistant reveals about student learning in microbiology
abstractText: Course-aligned artificial intelligence (AI) tutors are increasingly offered as learning support in higher education. Beyond providing practice and feedback, they may also help teachers identify gaps in understanding across a cohort. In a second-year medical microbiology and immunology unit of 500 to 800 students, a course-aligned AI assistant built on The University of Sydney’s Cogniti platform gave students scenario-based short-answer practice with rubric-referenced feedback. Its conversation logs turned out to be a diagnostic instrument. Across more than 1300 conversations, the logs revealed cohort-level knowledge gaps and recurring terminology errors mid-semester. An exploratory analysis also found small positive correlations between practice-oriented use of the assistant and final short-answer marks, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously. The gaps were fed back to the class through an interactive revision resource used in lectures. These insights could be obtained through three approaches requiring different levels of technical expertise: the platform’s own no-code summaries, method-led coding with basic programming, and specialist computational analysis. We also discuss how the approach can be adapted where no equivalent platform exists. The project highlights that a course-aligned AI assistant can provide valuable insight into cohort-level understanding of the subject.

title: Implementation of Heuristic Dispatching Rule in Monte Carlo Tree Search: Scheduling Machines
abstractText: The Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP) is a classical NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem in which minimizing makespan becomes increasingly challenging as problem size increases. Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) has emerged as a promising optimization approach; however, its reliance on random rollouts can produce suboptimal schedules characterized by substantial machine idle time. This study aimed to integrate heuristic dispatching rules into MCTS to improve scheduling performance on the Taillard ta20 benchmark instance, comprising 20 jobs and 15 machines. Two heuristic-guided variants, MCTS + EDD and MCTS + LDD, were developed by incorporating the Giffler–Thompson conflict-set procedure and an ?-greedy selection strategy (? = 0.1). Their performance was compared with that of baseline MCTS using 1,000, 2,000, and 3,000 rollouts, with 10 independent runs per configuration. Performance was evaluated based on average makespan, best makespan, standard deviation, computation time, and schedule feasibility. At 3,000 rollouts, MCTS + EDD and MCTS + LDD reduced average makespan by 15.78% and 20.20%, respectively, relative to the baseline MCTS average of 2,369.40. Both heuristic-guided variants also exhibited lower variability, with standard deviations ranging from 15.12 to 36.91, compared with 41.86 to 58.07 for baseline MCTS. Furthermore, the heuristic-guided methods achieved higher machine utilization rates of 51.39% (EDD) and 54.53% (LDD), compared with 44.40% for baseline MCTS. All best-performing schedules satisfied the evaluated scheduling constraints. These findings demonstrated that incorporating heuristic dispatching rules improved scheduling performance and consistency within the tested configurations. Notably, MCTS + LDD with 1,000 rollouts achieved a lower makespan than baseline MCTS with 3,000 rollouts while requiring less computation time, suggesting that heuristic guidance offered greater performance benefits than increasing the rollout budget alone under the experimental conditions.

title: Direct Measurement of the Quantum Capacitance in Oxide Semiconductors Using an Electric-Field-Penetration Technique
abstractText: Abstract Indium-based oxide semiconductor (OS) field-effect transistors (FETs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation monolithic three-dimensional (3D) integration, but a limited understanding of channel capacitance hinders further scaling. Here, we measure quantum capacitance (Cq) in In-based OS channels by using a lock-in-based electric-field-penetration technique (eFPT). A small AC voltage modulation superimposed on the back-gate DC bias induces an electric field at the top gate, detected as an AC current (ITG). Normalizing this current to its full depletion reference (ITG0) enables Cq extraction. Linear current scaling with frequency, excitation amplitude, and device area, together with an invariant normalized response, supports robust capacitance extraction. In the accumulation regime, an increase in Cq with DC bias is observed, which is consistent with band nonparabolicity and occupation of higher energy subbands. Finally, thicker InOx channels and higher In concentrations in InGaZnO (IGZO) films exhibit a larger Cq. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of tailoring Cq in In-based OS FETs.

abstractText: Trong bối cảnh Hà Nội sắp xếp lại đơn vị hành chính và triển khai mô hình chính quyền địa phương hai cấp, việc đánh giá khả năng cung cấp các hoạt động phòng, chống và quản lý bệnh đái tháo đường (ĐTĐ) tại tuyến y tế cơ sở là cần thiết để định hướng phân bổ nguồn lực. Có 88,9% TYT triển khai dịch vụ quản lý/điều trị ĐTĐ thuộc phạm vi bảo hiểm y tế (BHYT). Thiết bị xét nghiệm đường huyết nhanh có tại 75,4% TYT; 41,3% TYT báo cáo thiết bị này đủ phục vụ hoạt động chuyên môn. title: Quasi-Mittag-Leffler synchronization of delayed fractional-order Cohen-Grossberg inertial neural networks with uncertain parameters
abstractText: In this work, the quasi-Mittag-Leffler (QML) synchronization problem of fractional-order Cohen–Grossberg inertial neural networks (FOCGINNs) in the presence of uncertain parameters and time-varying delays is investigated. Initially, two control strategies, namely, a state-feedback controller and an adaptive controller, are developed to achieve QML synchronization. By employing these control strategies, sufficient synchronization conditions are established using Lyapunov stability theory in connection with the fractional-order Halanay inequality and the Razumikhin approach. Moreover, explicit synchronization error bounds are derived using the Mittag–Leffler function. Finally, numerical simulations validate the theoretical results, demonstrating the effectiveness of both controllers and confirming the robustness of the proposed synchronization framework.

abstractText: Vocabulary knowledge is foundational to learning Arabic in primary school, where reliance on rote memorization can contribute to boredom and poor retention. Research on digital gamification has focused mainly on quantitative outcomes in coeducational settings, leaving engagement in girls-only classrooms at primary madrasahs affiliated with Islamic boarding schools (pesantren) underexplored. This study examined how Wordwall was used to teach animal vocabulary (mufradāt ḥayawān) and how girls engaged behaviorally, cognitively, and affectively. The descriptive qualitative case study focused on 29 girls in Grade 3, Section B, at MI Nurul Mun’im. Data were collected through structured participant observation, in-depth teacher interviews, student focus groups, and instructional documentation and analyzed using the interactive framework of Miles et al. (2014). Using a shared classroom display, students progressed through three Wordwall activities (Match Up, Random Wheel, and Quiz), creating a more active and collaborative learning environment. Active participation, group quiz accuracy, and individual vocabulary mastery reached 93.1%, 88.5%, and 86.2%, respectively. Students also showed less anxiety about speaking Arabic. The findings suggest that whole-class digital gamification can support engagement and vocabulary learning, with potential benefits for reducing extraneous cognitive load and supporting retention over time. The study offers an adaptable model for integrating digital gamification into pesantren-affiliated madrasahs with single-sex classrooms and restrictions on personal devices.

Functional and lncRNA changes in ovine blood monocytes and derived macrophages following paratuberculosis vaccination
abstractText: Abstract Vaccination is central to control paratuberculosis in ruminants. Commercial vaccines such as Gudair ® , although not fully preventing infection, reduce clinical signs and faecal shedding. Nevertheless, their protective immunological mechanisms remain unclear. This study evaluated the effect of Gudair ® vaccination on mononuclear phagocyte function in sheep ( Ovis aries ) and correlated it with their long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) expression. Ten Assaf lambs were divided into vaccinated ( n = 5) and non-vaccinated ( n = 5) groups. Peripheral blood was collected before vaccination and at 30-, 60- and 90-days post-vaccination (dpv) to assess antigen-specific IFN-γ and antibody responses. Phagocytosis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production were evaluated in the monocyte fraction following in vitro Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (Map) infection of whole blood. At 90 dpv, monocytes were also isolated from peripheral blood to generate ovine monocyte-derived macrophages (OvMDMs) to assess Map phagocytosis and intracellular survival and lncRNAs expression analysis by RNA-seq. Vaccination induced increased IFN-γ and anti-Map antibody responses over time. Monocytes from vaccinated lambs showed significantly higher ROS production at 90 dpv ( p < 0.05), whereas phagocytosis did not differ between groups. No significant differences were observed in OvMDMs regarding Map phagocytosis or bacterial survival. Transcriptome analysis of monocytes at 90 dpv identified 6854 lncRNAs (4719 annotated and 2135 novel), of which four were differentially expressed between groups. Cis- and trans-based computational analyses identified potential associations with genes involved in immune-related pathways. These findings improve our understanding of the innate immune responses induced by paratuberculosis vaccination and identify candidate lncRNAs for further investigation in vaccine-induced immunity.

A Review of Strategies to Improve Rater Consistency in EFL Writing Assessment
abstractText: As interest in second language writing assessment has grown, the role of raters has come under increasing scrutiny. Although raters aim to score fairly, research consistently shows variation in severity and scoring patterns. This narrative literature review synthesizes studies on rater bias in EFL writing assessment and evaluates strategies for improving consistency. Five main approaches are considered: rater training, using multiple raters, avoiding rater fatigue, rubric development, and Multi-Faceted Rasch Measurement (MFRM). Each is discussed in terms of its benefits, limitations, and practical applications. The paper also distinguishes between intra-rater and inter-rater consistency, examines how bias appears in classroom, institutional, and large-scale testing contexts, and considers the broader implications for teachers, institutions, and test developers. The review concludes that no single strategy can eliminate inconsistency, but combining approaches offers the most effective path toward reducing bias and promoting fairness in EFL writing assessment.

title: Morphometric and ecological correlates of phalangeal elongation in extant arboreal mammals and implication for inferring arboreality in fossils
abstractText: Abstract Arboreality is thought to represent an ancestral condition in mammals and was associated with various morphological adaptations such as limb elongation. Here we investigate the relationship between intrinsic digit proportions (phalangeal index, PI) and arboreality across 205 extant and 49 fossil mammalian taxa. Using phylogenetic comparative methods, we tested correlations between fore- and hindfoot PIs, body mass and a proxy for arboreality defined as relative time spent in trees. Results show that arboreal species exhibit higher PIs than non-arboreal taxa, confirming that phalangeal elongation is a key functional adaptation to arboreal environments. Contrary to expectations, primates do not display the highest PIs; instead, marsupials and sloths exhibit the greatest phalangeal elongation, highlighting widespread convergent evolution. Forefoot PIs are negatively correlated with body mass, whereas both fore- and hindfoot PIs are positively correlated with time spent in trees, with variations between phylogenetic groups. Using our model to infer the time spent in trees in fossil taxa reveals that extinct species exhibit a high variability in phalangeal elongation, associated with possible early ‘hyperarborealism’. Overall, our findings demonstrate that elongated digits are a generalized and ancestral adaptive response to arboreal locomotion rather than an euarchontans-specific innovation.

While slow freezing is an established technique, vitrification offers a practical, field-adaptable alternative, particularly relevant for the Antillean manatee. Therefore, optimizing vitrification protocols and cryoprotectant combinations is essential for establishing dermal tissue banks. This study evaluated two vitrification techniques (direct cover vitrification, DCV, and direct vitrification in cryovials, DVC) using two intracellular cryoprotectant concentrations (3.0 M or 6.0 M ethylene glycol and dimethyl sulfoxide) for Antillean manatee dermis cryopreservation. Non-cryopreserved tissues and slow-frozen samples served as controls. All groups were assessed by histological and ultrastructural analyses and their ability to support fibroblast recovery. Histological evaluations showed that fibroblast density was preserved in DCV at both concentrations, with results comparable to fresh tissue and slow freezing. The collagen matrix was preserved only in DCV-6 M, whereas all vitrification protocols maintained normal elastic fiber organization. Despite preserving tissue architecture, fibroblast recovery was successful only in non-cryopreserved and slow-frozen samples, while vitrified tissues failed to support cell proliferation. Although DCV, particularly at 6 M, effectively preserves dermal structure, the tested vitrification protocols were insufficient to ensure fibroblast recovery.

title: Motivaciones económicas, personales y sociales para emprender en estudiantes de Contaduría Pública de una Universidad Pública de Tabasco, México
abstractText: El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar las motivaciones económicas, personales y sociales para emprender en estudiantes de la Licenciatura en Contaduría Pública de una facultad económico-administrativa de una universidad pública de Tabasco, México, así como su relación con algunas características sociodemográficas. Se realizó una investigación cuantitativa, no experimental, transversal, descriptiva y correlacional. Participaron 143 estudiantes que respondieron un cuestionario de 18 ítems con escala tipo Likert de cuatro puntos. El instrumento obtuvo un alfa de Cronbach de .914. Las motivaciones personales registraron la media más alta (3.281), seguidas de las económicas (3.213) y las sociales (3.083). No se encontraron diferencias estadísticamente significativas entre hombres y mujeres en ninguna de las tres dimensiones. Las motivaciones personales y sociales presentaron la correlación más alta (r = .692; p < .01). Además, el semestre cursado mostró correlaciones positivas con las motivaciones personales (r = .290; p < .01) y económicas (r = .230; p < .01). Los resultados muestran que los estudiantes valoran principalmente los aspectos personales del emprendimiento y que las tres dimensiones de motivación se relacionan entre sí.

Making Learning Meaningful: A Task-Based Approach to Legal Translation Instruction
abstractText: This research adopted a case-study methodology based on document analysis to examine the integration of meaningful learning and the task-based approach as a means of improving instruction and competence acquisition among future legal translators. A specialized translator must master the terminology and structures of a technical field to solve translation problems. In legal translation, translators must be able to manage specialized legal terminology and complex structures. They also need an in-depth understanding of the legal systems associated with the source and target languages (Cao, 2007; Hurtado Albir, 2001; Kiraly, 2000; Prieto Ramos, 2014). The study examined a population of legal translation students in a public university located in northeastern Mexico. The research instruments and sources included authentic documents, analysis of translation portfolios, surveys, and a review of course syllabi. The outcomes demonstrated a positive correlation between authentic tasks and greater proficiency of legal language among participants, providing evidence of meaningful learning through the resolution of real-world problems and the development of knowledge in legal translation resulting in the integration of authentic texts, a gradual increase in assignment difficulty, the application of methodologies and theoretical foundations of translation, the use of computer-assisted translation tools, and continuous feedback from the professors and peers that foster the acquisition of specialized knowledge and the development of professional competencies in legal translation practice.
