title: The Monogamous Screen: Ripley, Attention Warfare, and the Seduction of ‘Quality’
abstractText: Steven Zaillian’s Ripley (2024) wages attention warfare against the distracted, second screen behaviors of the contemporary streaming audience. This article argues that the series constructs a monogamous screen, demanding an exclusive relationship with the image to validate itself as quality TV. Employing a multimodal formalist analysis, I examine how Ripley utilizes forensic aesthetics to transform settings into fields of evidence, employs acoustic aggression to physically implicate the listener, and highlights the drudgery of evil to deny narrative shortcuts. Additionally, Andrew Scott’s performance is analyzed as a glitching algorithm that enforces forensic vigilance. Ultimately, the article contends that this aesthetic hostility functions as a gatekeeping mechanism, commodifying the luxury of focus as a marker of superior taste within the attention economy.

title: Study on the Wetting Properties of Coal Dust Based on Sedimentation Behavior and Selection of Optimal Surfactants
abstractText: Abstract Spray dust suppression in coal mines relies on the wetting of coal particles by the spray liquid. Most screening tests, however, assess only the first droplet–coal contact, although in practice coal dust undergoes repeated wetting, drying, and rewetting. A sedimentation-based protocol then treats initial wetting and the rewetting of dried, modified coal dust in deionized water as two independent dimensions. Twelve monomeric surfactants of four classes were screened at six concentrations (0.02–0.20 wt %), and the best were blended in equal volumes. Coal dust of two size fractions (d ≤ 0.150 and 0.075 mm) from the Chengzihe Coal Mine was tested, with the settling rate as a dynamic wetting proxy. Surfactant ranking differed between the stages and reversed with particle size, so a single contact measurement cannot predict field performance. A reproducible inflection at 0.04–0.06 wt % defined a practical concentration range. For coarse dust, monomers generally outperformed the blends (OP-10 and FPA-T strongest in initial wetting); for fine dust, the blends were superior, and FPA-T+AOS was the only system effective in both stages, making it the most suitable additive for the fine fraction. Contact angle, FTIR, and zeta potential explained this static–dynamic mismatch, providing a particle-size-dependent basis for additive selection.

Genome sequence data for 16 bongkrekic acid-producing Burkholderia gladioli pv. cocovenenans strains isolated from retail wood ear samples in China
abstractText: Abstract Objectives Burkholderia gladioli pv. cocovenenans is a foodborne bacterium that produces bongkrekic acid. This toxin is associated with severe food poisoning. In China, wood ear products have been linked to such cases. However, genome data from food-derived isolates remain limited. Data description Sixteen toxigenic isolates were obtained from 65 retail wood ear samples. Samples were collected from markets in Fuyang, Anhui Province, China, and from online stores. The isolates were identified as B. gladioli using VITEK MS. The presence of bon genes was assessed by real-time PCR, and bongkrekic acid production was confirmed by LC-MS/MS. Whole-genome sequencing was performed using the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. Raw reads were filtered using fastp. Draft genomes were assembled using SPAdes. GTDB-Tk classified all 16 isolates as B. gladioli . The draft genome sizes ranged from approximately 8.15 to 8.50 Mb, with GC contents of approximately 68%. Genome completeness was 100%, and contamination ranged from 2.33% to 3.86% based on CheckM2 analysis. Raw reads and genome assemblies were deposited in the NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA) and GenBank under BioProject accessions PRJNA1475073 and PRJNA1475080, respectively. A curated dataset with genome metadata, assembly statistics, and pairwise ANI values was deposited in Figshare.

Studi Eksperimental Zeolit sebagai Pengganti Sebagian Semen terhadap Kuat Tekan Self-Compacting Concrete (SCC)
abstractText: Abstract This study aims to evaluate the mix design, fresh concrete properties, and compressive strength development of Self-Compacting Concrete (SCC) utilizing natural zeolite as a partial cement replacement. The zeolite substitution ratios were set at 0%, 5%, 10%, 12.5%, and 15% by weight of cement, targeting a specified compressive strength of 45 MPa at 28 days. The mix proportions were developed based on SNI 03-6468-2000 in conjunction with Okamura's method and Bina Marga SKh.1.7.23 specifications. Slump flow tests were conducted to determine fresh workability, while compressive strength tests on 10x20 cm cylindrical specimens were performed at ages of 7, 14, and 28 days. The results revealed that increasing zeolite content reduced slump flow due to the higher water absorption and specific surface area of zeolite particles. The mixtures with 0%, 5%, and 10% zeolite achieved slump flow values of 60 cm, 58 cm, and 58 cm, respectively, complying with the EFNARC Class SF1 criteria. Conversely, the 12.5% and 15% mixtures failed to meet the flowability thresholds. Regarding hardened properties, the 10% zeolite replacement yielded optimum mechanical performance, achieving a 28-day compressive strength of 42.43 MPa (a 4.05% increase compared to the 40.78 MPa control). Exceeding 10% zeolite replacement caused strength degradation due to the reduction of primary cementitious binder. Fracture behavior evaluation confirmed normal failure modes (cone, cone and split, cone and shear) across all test specimens. In conclusion, a 10% zeolite replacement ratio is identified as the optimum dosage that balances optimal workability and compressive strength in SCC.

title: Evaluating Psycho-Pedagogical Strategies to Reduce Foreign Language Anxiety Among Bukavu Secondary School Learners
abstractText: Foreign Language Anxiety (FLA) can hinder learners’ participation and engagement in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms. Although previous studies have examined FLA and anxiety-reduction strategies in Bukavu, empirical evidence on the effectiveness of structured interventions among secondary-school learners remains limited. This study evaluated a psycho-pedagogical intervention conducted at EDAP/ISP Bukavu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, from February to May 2025. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design involving experimental and control groups was employed. The control group comprised 48 pupils, while the experimental group included 42 pupils at pre-test and 46 at post-test. The findings revealed a descriptive reduction in mean FLA scores in the experimental group, from 3.08 to 2.86, compared with a slight decrease in the control group, from 3.19 to 3.17. However, the reduction in the experimental group was not statistically significant (p = .259). Descriptive analyses also revealed decreases in communication apprehension, fear of negative evaluation, test anxiety, and English classroom anxiety in the experimental group, with the largest reductions observed in communication apprehension and English classroom anxiety. These findings provide context-specific evidence on psycho-pedagogical approaches to FLA in secondary education, while highlighting the need for further research using robust comparative analyses to establish intervention effectiveness.
